findings.title: Migration crashes when no embed category is configured
findings.body: The category query can return no rows when embed_category is unset (its default is an empty string) or names a deleted category. Indexing [0]['id'] then dereferences nil before the uncategorized fallback is reached. This prevents migrations from completing on ordinary installations that have never configured embedding. Handle an empty result before accessing the row.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are not normalized for the new lookup
findings.body: The migration inserts old embeddable_hosts entries verbatim, bypassing the new model's normalization callback. The previous host check accepted entries such as http://eviltrout.com and https://eviltrout.com, but the new lookup compares the stored value directly with URI.host, which is only eviltrout.com. Those previously working configurations stop allowing embeds after upgrade, and the original settings are deleted. Normalize migrated entries to the same representation used by the new lookup.

findings.title: Hosts saved with ports can never match incoming URLs
findings.body: The host validator accepts values such as example.com:8080 and the normalization callback preserves the port, but record_for_host compares that value against uri.host, which excludes the port. Thus a host successfully added as example.com:8080 will reject even http://example.com:8080 and will not supply its configured category to imports. Make storage and lookup agree on how ports are handled.

findings.title: Host validation rejects valid longer top-level domains
findings.body: The new format validation restricts the final domain label to two through five letters. Valid hosts such as example.museum or example.technology therefore cannot be added or saved in the embedding editor, although the previous host setting and lookup had no such restriction. Use hostname validation that supports valid longer top-level domains.
